findings.topic: Atomic native ownership and bounded draining
findings.details: CreateProcessW uses JOB_LIST and HANDLE_LIST atomically with a noninheritable kill-on-close private job and suspended initial thread; resumes after reader readiness. Normal parent exit and timeout terminate that job, verify active processes zero, and drain/cancel fixed-buffer readers within the shared 3-second grace. Startup/capture failures fail closed with no process-name kill or uncontained fallback.

One lower-only 120000-ms image context begins before stable source snapshot and covers frame/colour/ICC queries, all conversion/validation phases and retry waits. Five limits precede reads; a final remaining-time check gates no-overwrite move. Installed stricter policy stays effective. Timeout/resource/unsafe-tree outcomes stop that item and preserve sibling processing.

findings.topic: Temporary ownership, setup order and unsafe-tree preservation
findings.details: Existing regular canonical plain temporary root <=160 characters, no linked ancestors and physical source overlap rejection are validated before destination write probe. Exclusive per-image cache directory uses child-only environment. Candidate/ICC/snapshot staging stays on output volume. Unconfirmed returned TreeTerminated is directly rejected and makes CleanupSafe=false sticky; all item scratch is preserved. Confirmed cleanup is nonrecursive and only regular reserved magick-* names are eligible.

Exactly eight declared paths changed. BAT, CI workflow, bootstrap/dependencies and profile assets remain unchanged. Public positional forms, exact cap, six scales, colour/alpha/frame policy, literal filename guards, source/no-overwrite, timestamps, duplicates and video paths remain within existing contracts. Real Ctrl+C and cancellation remain M3-T03 scope.

Seventeen cases use owned benign compiled processes, independent Toolhelp direct-parent/PID-creation identities, held handles and real pinned native siblings. Covers descendant-held pipes after parent exit, floods, valid JPEG before stall, unrelated ImageMagick survival/completion, real constrained cache, stricter private copied policy, cumulative phases, exact source/namespace preservation and setup boundaries. Unconfirmed-kill flag is controlled after actual successful kill and explicitly qualified.

Current measurement trace delegates the actual bounded observer path and retains resource/environment/shared-budget traces; historical image algorithms retain their flags while using the captured current wrapper to avoid type overload collision. Only leading limit triplets are separated from core image flags. Both successful tiny smokes bind the final runtime 791e8484... and final adapter bytes; initial square-fixture ambiguity and raw controller dimension-label erratum remain preserved. No representative quality/performance benchmark rerun is claimed.

D30/I12 cite official Windows atomic job and cancellation semantics, pinned ImageMagick resource/JPEG source and dated current upstream notices. Pin 7.1.2-32 meets the declared reviewed patched versions. No crafted exploit execution, generic sandbox certification or owner quality approval is asserted.

limitations: Pixel-cache ceilings do not cap every decoder/delegate heap allocation or arbitrary file writes; these are practical defenses, not an exploit-proof sandbox.
Synchronous filesystem copying/creation is counted where specified but not preemptible; termination and drain grace can extend wall time.

Reserved magick-* names in the exclusive cache namespace cannot distinguish concurrent same-pattern external arrivals; hostile filesystem mutation is outside this containment check.
Unsupported JOB_LIST/HANDLE_LIST or incompatible inherited-job restrictions fail closed, rather than falling back.

implementation_notes: An image now shares a 120,000-ms elapsed budget across its snapshot, frame/colour/ICC queries, conversion attempts, retries and complete JPEG validation. The final move requires time remaining. Every real image command requests process-local pixel-cache memory 512 MiB, map 1 GiB, disk 2 GiB, two threads and the remaining seconds; stricter installed ImageMagick policies still apply. A timeout or resource failure rejects that image and continues later usable image/video siblings with application warning/partial code 2.

Native processes are created atomically inside a private kill-on-close Windows job and start only after two bounded stream readers are ready. Cleanup targets that job, confirms an empty tree and drains/cancels readers within one 3-second grace; it never selects unrelated processes by name or PID snapshots. The separate exclusive plain TEMP cache root is validated before output writes and kept outside the physical source tree. Media snapshots, ICC data and JPEG candidates keep output-volume staging. Unconfirmed tree termination rejects finalization and preserves all item scratch; ordinary cleanup is nonrecursive, removes only regular magick-* cache files and preserves unexpected entries with a warning.

D30/I12 record the implementation policy and dated official Windows/ImageMagick advisory review. Public positional/BAT calls, exact size cap, six scales, JPEG/colour/white-alpha/frame selection, literal paths, no-overwrite transactions, source preservation, video bytes and successful duplicate retention remain within their existing contracts. The development Measure-SizeQuality trace now follows the current bounded native observer and separates leading resource-limit arguments from core image flags. Tiny compatibility checks are separate from representative quality/performance measurement and owner approval.
limitations: Windows 10/Server 2016 JOB_LIST support and compatible inherited-job restrictions are required. Unsupported atomic assignment fails closed. ImageMagick memory/map/disk limits govern pixel cache, not every decoder/delegate heap allocation or arbitrary write; these controls do not certify an exploit-proof sandbox.

The shared clock counts image-copy/retry elapsed time, but synchronous filesystem calls are not preemptible. Native termination/drain grace can add wall time. ImageMagick's own time limit is cooperative and SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH can disable it; the external wrapper deadline remains the native-hang authority. A noncooperative kernel driver can still delay completion of an I/O cancellation request; incomplete capture never permits finalization.

Cleanup assumes the exclusively allocated cache namespace remains trustworthy. A concurrent regular magick-* arrival is indistinguishable from a native cache file; foreign names, directories and reparse entries remain with warnings. Unconfirmed termination preservation was tested with a controlled returned flag after an actual successfully terminated tree, not by reproducing an OS failure to kill.

Development targets, saved API/resource probes and tiny 128x160 measurement smokes retain their own raw source/artifact bindings. They are separate from clean-I full normal/control and hosted acceptance. No representative benchmark rerun, quality/performance improvement, owner aesthetic approval or codec-wide exploit test is inferred. Existing HEIC still-collection and independent colour-reference qualifications remain in their original evidence.

The unrelated-process fixture uses a declared first synthetic image as its completion oracle; RGB stdin only keeps the process blocked until synchronization ends, and all stdin-derived frames are discarded. Actual default and forced-BOM controls passed on both shells. The original hosted stdin bytes were not recorded, so its BOM explanation remains a supported inference. Repaired-revision full normal/control and hosted gates require their own immutable evidence.

Real Ctrl+C/cooperative cancellation, interrupted-copy exit behavior and force-termination recovery remain M3-T03. This card stops after M3-T02 acceptance; releases, deployment and owner acceptance stay separate.
